overview.executive_summary: This news cycle is dominated by active exploitation of critical edge and infrastructure systems, including FortiMail and Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager. Major incidents also include the theft of Pentagon personnel records, a $387.5 million cryptocurrency loss, and an AI-assisted breach involving Zammad zero-days. Attackers continue to exploit trusted platforms, exposed credentials, remote-management tools, and widely deployed operational technology. Organizations should prioritize known exploited vulnerabilities, investigate possible compromise, and review access controls around sensitive systems.

sections.heading: CISA Adds Fortinet FortiMail Flaw to Exploited Vulnerability Catalog
sections.what_happened: CISA added CVE-2026-104286, a Fortinet FortiMail path traversal vulnerability, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities Catalog based on evidence of active exploitation. BleepingComputer reports that Fortinet warned the flaw is being exploited in zero-day attacks to execute unauthorized code or commands on vulnerable devices.
sections.why_it_matters: FortiMail systems may be exposed to active attacks, creating risks of unauthorized access or system compromise.
sections.recommended_attention: Prioritize remediation of affected FortiMail systems and investigate whether exposed devices show signs of compromise.

sections.heading: Attackers Exploit Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager Authentication Bypass
sections.what_happened: Cisco warned that attackers are exploiting CVE-2026-76504, a critical authentication-bypass flaw in Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager. The vulnerability can allow a remote attacker without login access to use the Manager API as the administrator, and CISA added it to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities Catalog.
sections.why_it_matters: Compromise of SD-WAN management infrastructure could give attackers administrative control over network-management functions.
sections.recommended_attention: Apply fixed releases and review SD-WAN Manager access, authentication activity, and administrative actions.

sections.heading: Hackers Stole Pentagon Personnel Records of Over 3 Million People
sections.what_happened: The Pentagon's Defense Manpower Data Center is notifying millions of military service members that hackers stole their data after breaching the Pentagon's human resources management system in October 2025. The reported affected population exceeds 3 million people.
sections.why_it_matters: The incident involves a large volume of personnel information connected to military service members.
sections.recommended_attention: Affected organizations and individuals should monitor notification details and assess exposure of personnel records and related systems.

sections.heading: Bitget Confirms Third-Party Zero-Day Behind $387.5 Million Cryptocurrency Theft
sections.what_happened: Bitget confirmed that attackers who stole $387.5 million the previous week exploited a zero-day flaw in third-party security products. The investigation also recovered a customized tool used by the attacker.
sections.why_it_matters: The incident demonstrates how weaknesses in third-party security products can enable extremely costly cryptocurrency theft.
sections.recommended_attention: Review third-party security dependencies, investigate the affected environment, and monitor for related attacker tooling.

sections.heading: Police Dismantle KillSec Ransomware Gang Allegedly Led by 16-Year-Old
sections.what_happened: An international law-enforcement operation called Operation KillSwitch seized KillSec's data-leak site and servers, led to three arrests, and identified a 16-year-old as the group's alleged administrator. The Hacker News reports that police in Spain arrested the suspected operator and took control of the leak site.
sections.why_it_matters: The operation disrupts a ransomware group accused of stealing organizational data and threatening publication unless victims paid.
sections.recommended_attention: Organizations should continue monitoring for KillSec-related extortion activity and preserve relevant evidence if targeted.

sections.heading: DIVD Says Zammad Zero-Days Enabled AI-Driven Network Breach
sections.what_happened: The Dutch Institute for Vulnerability Disclosure said its network breach was possible through a chain of two zero-day vulnerabilities in the open-source Zammad ticketing system. The report describes the breach as AI-driven.
sections.why_it_matters: A zero-day chain in a ticketing platform can expose internal support data and provide attackers with access to organizational networks.
sections.recommended_attention: Review Zammad deployments, investigate unusual activity, and follow vendor or disclosure guidance associated with the flaws.

sections.heading: Over 543,000 Valid Credentials Exposed in Public GitHub Repositories
sections.what_happened: More than 543,000 credentials exposed in public GitHub repositories were still valid in July despite platform security measures intended to prevent accidental leaks of sensitive data.
sections.why_it_matters: Valid exposed credentials can enable unauthorized access across developer, cloud, and enterprise environments.
sections.recommended_attention: Search public repositories for active secrets, revoke exposed credentials, and strengthen secret-scanning and rotation processes.

sections.heading: Citrix NetScaler Post-Exploitation Payload Creates Superuser
sections.what_happened: Threat actors were observed exploiting a critical pre-authentication command-injection vulnerability in Citrix NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway to drop web shells and attempt to steal configuration data. Researchers observed malicious NetScaler payloads across multiple customer environments.
sections.why_it_matters: NetScaler appliances are exposed access infrastructure, so compromise can support persistence, configuration theft, and further intrusion.
sections.recommended_attention: Inspect NetScaler systems for web shells, unexpected superuser activity, and configuration-data access.

sections.heading: Armatura One Vulnerabilities Could Compromise Physical Access-Control Systems
sections.what_happened: CISA reported that vulnerabilities in Armatura LLC Armatura One could allow unauthorized database access, arbitrary code execution with the highest host privileges, or control of the physical access-control system. Affected versions include Armatura One below 4.7.2 and Armatura One USA below 4.6.1, with a listed CVSS score of 9.8.
sections.why_it_matters: The affected product is deployed worldwide across communications, critical manufacturing, energy, and transportation sectors, and compromise could affect both information systems and physical access.
sections.recommended_attention: Identify affected deployments, apply the listed updates, and review access-control and host logs for unauthorized activity.

sections.heading: Monta Charging-Station Platform Vulnerabilities Enable Unauthorized Control
sections.what_happened: CISA reported vulnerabilities in Monta monta.app that could allow attackers to gain unauthorized administrative control over vulnerable charging stations or disrupt charging services through denial-of-service attacks. The issues include missing authentication for critical functions and insufficiently protected credentials, with a listed CVSS score of 9.4.
sections.why_it_matters: The platform supports charging infrastructure in energy and transportation contexts, where unauthorized control or service disruption could affect operations.
sections.recommended_attention: Identify affected charging-station deployments, restrict management interfaces, and prioritize vendor remediation.

stories.title: CISA Adds One Known Exploited Vulnerability to Catalog

Fortinet separately warned that the flaw is being exploited in zero-day attacks to execute unauthorized code or commands on vulnerable devices.
stories.why_it_matters: Active exploitation makes affected FortiMail systems an immediate remediation and investigation priority.

stories.title: Cisco Warns of Attackers Exploiting Critical Authentication Bypass in SD-WAN Manager
stories.summary: Attackers are exploiting CVE-2026-76504, a critical Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager authentication-bypass flaw. Cisco said an unauthenticated remote attacker could use the Manager API as the administrator; fixed releases are available and there is no workaround.
stories.why_it_matters: Unauthorized administrative access to SD-WAN management could expose network-control functions.

stories.why_it_matters: The breach involves a large volume of personnel records associated with military service members.

tts.text: Here’s today’s cybersecurity briefing. First up, Fortinet FortiMail is under active attack: CISA added a critical path-traversal flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, so affected organizations should patch and investigate immediately. Cisco is also warning about active exploitation of an authentication bypass in Catalyst SD-WAN Manager, which could give an unauthenticated attacker administrator-level API access. On the incident side, hackers stole Pentagon personnel records belonging to more than three million people, while Bitget confirmed that a third-party zero-day was behind a 387.5-million-dollar cryptocurrency theft. Law enforcement disrupted the KillSec ransomware group, seizing its leak site and servers and arresting three people. One thing to keep an eye on is the reported Zammad breach, where two zero-days were allegedly used in an AI-driven attack. And there’s a basic but serious exposure problem: more than 543,000 credentials found in public GitHub repositories were still valid. Finally, critical infrastructure remains in focus, with Armatura One flaws potentially affecting physical access-control systems and Monta vulnerabilities threatening electric-vehicle charging operations. The immediate priorities are known exploited flaws, exposed credentials, and unusual activity on management systems.
